item.title: Take Me Group and Gett strike UK corporate ground transport partnership
item.description: Take Me Group Ltd has announced a strategic partnership with corporate ground travel platform Gett, aiming to strengthen the delivery of compliant and scalable transport services for business customers across the UK. The agreement brings together Take Me’s expanding regional operating footprint with Gett’s corporate booking and travel management technology. item.title: Mayor of London pledges to work with taxi trade to minimise the impact of driverless vehicles as policy develops
item.description: Image credit: LEVC The Mayor of London has pledged to work with the taxi industry and trade unions to minimise the impact of driverless vehicle technology on jobs and livelihoods, as questions continue over how automated passenger services could affect the capital’s black cab trade. item.title: Aberdeen taxi licensing review to consider easing street knowledge test for private hire drivers
item.description: Aberdeen City Council is preparing to review its Taxi and Private Hire Policy, with a proposed consultation set to examine whether the city’s Street Knowledge Test is limiting the growth of app-based private hire services such as Uber. According to the AGCC , a report due to go before the council’s Licensing Committee recommends launching a formal public consultation that would include a reassessment of the requirement for all taxi and private hire drivers to pass the Street Knowledge Test...

item.title: DfT signals they are still ‘considering further action’ on cross-border private hire enforcement as MPs raise licensing question
item.description: The Department for Transport (DfT) has acknowledged ongoing concerns over the ability of local authorities to effectively enforce standards against private hire vehicles licensed in one area but operating predominantly in another, as pressure grows for stronger national controls. item.title: Newcastle Airport opens off-site taxi waiting zone ahead of six million passenger target
item.description: Image credit: Newcastle Airport Newcastle Airport has opened a new off-site Waiting Zone for taxis, private vehicles and the public as it prepares for passenger numbers to reach a record six million in 2026. The facility, located at Callerton Parkway next to the Metro station, allows taxis, minibuses and public vehicles to wait for up to 90 minutes free of charge before collecting passengers. item.title: North Herts Council runs lone female night-time mystery shopper taxi operation
item.description: North Herts Council has carried out a targeted night-time safeguarding operation at Hitchin Railway Station to assess how licensed taxi drivers respond to potentially vulnerable female passengers during evening hours. The operation took place on Wednesday 10 December and was led by the council’s Licensing and Community Safety teams, supported by community volunteers. item.title: Rushcliffe Borough Council urges use of licensed taxis and private hire vehicles during festive surge
item.description: Rushcliffe Borough Council has issued a safety reminder to residents and visitors to only use licensed taxis and private hire vehicles when travelling during the festive period, citing an expected rise in demand over Christmas and New Year. The council is advising passengers to either pre-book journeys with a licensed private hire operator or use a licensed Hackney carriage from an authorised taxi rank when travelling within the borough. item.title: Mayor says TfL are aware of legal gap when it comes to London taxis booked via apps
item.description: Transport for London (TfL) has acknowledged a lack of legal clarity over when a London taxi is deemed to be formally hired when a journey is booked through an app, highlighting a regulatory gap that remains unresolved more than a decade after app-based booking became widespread. item.title: WHERE’S THE VAT? Why your taxi receipt doesn’t often show VAT
item.description: Passengers submitting expense claims may ask why a taxi receipt does not show VAT. Despite the most recent media around ‘Taxi Tax’, in most cases, the answer is straightforward. The majority of UK taxi drivers are self-employed sole traders who operate below the VAT registration threshold and are therefore not registered for VAT. Under current UK rules, businesses only have to register for VAT if their taxable turnover exceeds £90,000 in a rolling 12-month period. Large numbers of licensed...

item.title: Hackney Support Fund: Greater Manchester taxi drivers urged to act quickly as £12,560 clean cab grants open
